checks.detail: the requested (256, 341, 1) grid becomes (320, 405, 1) after add_absorbing_bc(thickness=2.0), and Sample.ROI = [(32, 288), (32, 373), (0, 1)] recovers the original (256, 341, 1). Indexing the padded array with an un-padded mask raises IndexError, which is the mistake this check exists to prevent.
checks.name: add_absorbing_bc_pads_the_sample_and_records_the_region_of_interest

checks.detail: inside the disc Re(eps) in [2.250000, 2.250000] against n^2 = 2.25; outside, [1.000000, 1.000000] against 1.0
checks.name: the_real_permittivity_is_exactly_n_squared_on_both_sides

checks.detail: Im(eps) is at most 0.000e+00 inside Sample.ROI and reaches 0.500000 in the pad: the extinction is confined to the padding, so it cannot contaminate the physics.
checks.name: the_absorbing_boundary_does_not_reach_the_region_of_interest

checks.detail: solve() returns (320, 405, 1, 3), i.e. the spatial dimensions (320, 405, 1) followed by a trailing 3-component axis. Its own docstring says "the first (left-most) axis the polarization vector" -- that is wrong, and so is the input layout: the source current density must ALSO be component-last or the solver raises a broadcasting TypeError.
checks.name: the_solver_returns_a_component_LAST_field_contradicting_its_docstring

checks.detail: per-component energies [0.0, 0.0, 1.30606777020148e-05]: the same (E_z, E_y, E_x) ordering c11 and c12 establish for VectorField.u also holds for this solver's output, so the two halves of Chromatix at least agree with each other.
checks.name: an_x_polarized_source_produces_energy_only_in_component_index_2

checks.detail: mean |amplitude change| relative to the empty control is 0.000004 inside the disc and 0.000003 outside, against an interior reference amplitude of 0.000012. The scattering is real and concentrated on the object rather than spread over the domain.
checks.name: the_dielectric_disc_changes_the_field_and_does_so_locally

checks.detail: mean amplitude on the first two rows of the domain is 6.223491e-07 against an interior mean of 1.163277e-05, a ratio of 0.0535: the boundary condition is absorbing, so the solution is not dominated by wrap-around
checks.name: the_absorbing_boundary_suppresses_the_domain_edge

checks.detail: complex overlap 0.999441 and relative RMS difference 3.345e-02 between the memory-efficient fixed-point iteration and BiCGStab over Sample.ROI. These are different algorithms for the same linear system, so agreement is the strongest check available without an external oracle -- and neither upstream nor the docstring asserts it.
checks.name: the_fixed_point_and_bicgstab_solvers_agree

demonstrates: chromatix.experimental.modified_born_series: EmptySample, Source, add_absorbing_bc(sample, axis, thickness, max_extinction) and solve(sample, source, maxiter, tol, use_bicgstab) -- the only full-wave solver in Chromatix.
notes: chromatix.experimental.modified_born_series is the only full-wave solver in Chromatix and it lives under `experimental`. Upstream's example page truncates after the sample-construction cell, so the solve() call in this reproduction is written from the pinned signature rather than copied. The source construction (a polarization-first (3, *spatial) array with a line source at the entrance face) is this repository's choice; upstream shows no source cell.
title: Modified Born Series
